sources.agency: California Department of Health Care Services (DHCS)
sources.policyStatement: Medi-Cal will never ask for money to turn in a renewal. It will never cost money to apply for Medi-Cal, and no one can make you pay to turn in Medi-Cal applications, renewals, or proof. If someone asks for money to complete your renewal, report it to the Medi-Cal fraud hotline at (800) 822-6222.
sources.limitations: This applies to the Medi-Cal renewal process itself. Other health services may have separate costs such as Share of Cost for some beneficiaries.

sources.agency: California Department of Health Care Services (DHCS)
sources.policyStatement: You can turn in your Medi-Cal renewal online through BenefitsCal, by mail, by phone, or in person at your local Medi-Cal office. Not all members need to complete a renewal form. If you do, your local Medi-Cal office sends it in a bright yellow envelope, and you must complete it and turn in the information it asks for to keep your Medi-Cal.
sources.limitations: Renewal processes may vary slightly by county. Contact your local county office for specific procedures.

sources.agency: California Department of Health Care Services (DHCS)
sources.policyStatement: DHCS and your county social services office will never ask you to provide your Social Security number or passwords via text message, email, or phone call to maintain or renew your Medi-Cal coverage.
sources.limitations: Not found on dhcs.ca.gov when checked on 2026-10-25. The closest DHCS advice (Helpful Hints and Resources) is to never share your Social Security number or Medi-Cal details with anyone offering gifts or money. You may need to provide your SSN when applying through official channels. For EBT PINs, see the CDSS source.

sources.agency: California Department of Health Care Services (DHCS)
sources.policyStatement: Official Medi-Cal renewal information is on dhcs.ca.gov. To check your renewal date, turn in your renewal, or manage your benefits online, DHCS directs members to log in to BenefitsCal, or to KeepMediCalCoverage.org if they are not sure which account to use.
sources.limitations: County-specific websites also exist and are legitimate. This does not cover all legitimate government domains.

sources.agency: California Department of Health Care Services (DHCS)
sources.policyStatement: You still have Medi-Cal while your local Medi-Cal office reviews your renewal, and it only ends if you are no longer eligible. If your renewal is missing something, the office sends you a notice telling you what it needs. If your Medi-Cal ends because you did not turn in your form or information, you can turn it in within 90 days of the date on the letter without a new application.
sources.limitations: Specific timelines for responding may vary. Always respond to official county correspondence by the stated deadline.

sources.policyStatement: Each state's Medicaid agency runs Medicaid and CHIP for that state. To apply, see if you are eligible, get a replacement card, or check the status of your renewal, you must contact your state Medicaid agency. In California, that is the Department of Health Care Services (Medi-Cal).
sources.limitations: Federal guidance. Specific renewal procedures are determined by each state.

sources.policyStatement: Your county or the state will never text or call you requesting your EBT card number or PIN. CDSS may contact cardholders to encourage them to change their PIN, but will never ask for the cardholder's information by text message.
sources.limitations: Applies to EBT cards for CalFresh and CalWORKs, which CDSS runs, not to Medi-Cal. You may give your EBT card number when you yourself call your county welfare office or the EBT customer service line on the back of your card.
